record.original_question: Let T012(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which left stones are allowed, right stones are forbidden, and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that T012(3n+1, 3n+2) = 2^n n! for every n >= 1?

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.
Problem 3: Is it true that T012 (3n + 1, 3n + 2) = 2^n n! for n >= 1?
Comment: Colin Defant, Rupert Li, Benjamin Young and I worked on problem 2 during the conference and later succeeded in solving Problems 2 and 3; see [3].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix positive integers $a,b$. The $(a,b)$-benzel is a hexagonal region in the triangular grid defined by Propp, which is to be tiled by prototiles of five possible types: a "left stone", a "right stone", and three "bones" (tribones) corresponding to the three possible orientations of a $1\times 3$ rhombus tile on the triangular grid.

For $0\le i,j\le 1$ and $0\le k\le 3$, let $T_{ijk}(a,b)$ denote the number of tilings of the $(a,b)$-benzel using only prototiles from the set that contains the right stone iff $i=1$, contains the left stone iff $j=1$, and contains exactly $k$ of the three bones (with the choice of which $k$ orientations are allowed being part of the data, but the count $T_{ijk}$ understood as in the standard convention of the problem).

Prove or disprove: for every integer $n\ge 1$,
$$T_{012}(3n+1,\,3n+2) = 2^n\, n!.$$
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Defant, Li, Propp, and Young (e.g., "Tilings of Benzels via the Abacus Bijection", arXiv:2209.05717, and "Tilings of Benzels via Generalized Compression", arXiv:2403.07663) resolves several of Propp's benzel-tiling conjectures, including the formula in question for $T_{012}(3n+1, 3n+2)$.

status_evidence.title: Tilings of Benzels via the Abacus Bijection
status_evidence.snippet: Defant, Li, Propp, Young resolve enumerative conjectures concerning benzel tilings.
status_evidence.claim: The conjectured formula T_012(3n+1,3n+2)=2^n n! is established in follow-up work.

status_evidence.title: Tilings of Benzels via Generalized Compression
status_evidence.snippet: A generalized compression technique resolves additional conjectures of Propp on benzel tilings.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple benzel enumeration conjectures of Propp are settled.
